title: Modifying a DEA registration to change a name or address
rule_summary: ANY REGISTRANT MAY APPLY TO MODIFY ITS REGISTRATION to authorize the handling of additional controlled substances OR TO CHANGE ITS NAME OR ADDRESS by submitting a WRITTEN REQUEST to the DEA Registration Unit, and the request may also be submitted on-line. The request shall contain the registrant's name, address and registration number AS PRINTED ON THE CERTIFICATE OF REGISTRATION; the substances or schedules to be added, OR THE NEW NAME OR ADDRESS; and a signature in accordance with 21 CFR 1301.13(j). NO FEE is required for a modification, the request is HANDLED IN THE SAME MANNER AS AN APPLICATION FOR REGISTRATION, and if the modification is approved the Administrator issues a NEW CERTIFICATE OF REGISTRATION (DEA Form 223), which the registrant MAINTAINS WITH THE OLD CERTIFICATE UNTIL EXPIRATION.
exam_relevance: Tests the federal step a rebranding or relocating pharmacy owes alongside its Massachusetts filing: a name or address change is a modification of the existing DEA registration, not a new registration and not a fee-bearing application.
common_confusions: Treating a change of name or address as requiring a fresh DEA registration rather than a modification of the existing one.
Expecting a fee: no fee is required for a modification, though the request is handled in the same manner as an application for registration.
Discarding the old certificate of registration once the new one arrives, when the registrant maintains it with the old one until expiration.
verification_notes: Read in the current text of 21 CFR 1301.51 on the eCFR, displaying title 21 as of 9/10/2026, on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed.
